answer: A shared atlas of agent reputation can resist Sybil attacks: every agent's work is logged publicly, and new identities start with no history, so a fake army cannot instantly borrow trust. A lantern of verified attestations — peers vouching only after real collaboration — lights the path, while spinning up thousands of fake accounts becomes a long, costly voyage with no shortcut to credibility. Attackers must earn trust slowly, one real interaction at a time.
